definition: To achieve sudden, tremendous success or gain a large amount of money or advantage.
hinglishExplanation: Achanak bahut badi kamyabi, fayda ya dhan prapt karna.
example: With his revolutionary legal software, the young developer hit the jackpot.
contextNote: Aksar unanticipated ya dramatic success ke liye use hota hai.
keyDistinction: Dono similar hain, lekin 'hit the jackpot' lottery ya windfall sense mein zyada use hota hai.

definition: To succeed in reaching a goal, career height, or surviving a difficult ordeal.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi mushkil target ko achieve karna ya life mein safalta hasil karna.
example: After years of rigorous preparation, Sheela finally made it into the judicial academy.
contextNote: Context decide karta hai ki yeh career success hai ya survival.
keyDistinction: 'Make it' safalta darshata hai; 'make do' kisi tarah kaam chalane ko kehte hain.

definition: To make a successful beginning; to start developing or functioning smoothly.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi project ya scheme ka successfully shuru hona aur aage badhna.
example: The e-filing modernization project took months to get off the ground due to technical glitches.
contextNote: Early operational stage ke liye use hota hai.
keyDistinction: 'Get off the ground' shuru hone ke bare mein hai; 'hit the ground running' bina kisi delay ke fast pace par kaam karne ko kehte hain.

definition: To exhibit great talent and promise, destined to achieve high career success.
hinglishExplanation: Bahut tarakki karna ya aage chal kar bada naam kamana.
example: Given his analytical acumen and diligence, everyone knew the junior clerk would go places.
contextNote: Future potential aur promising career trajectory describe karta hai.
keyDistinction: 'Go places' bright future ke liye hai; 'go through the motions' bina interest ke formal duty poori karne ke liye hai.

definition: To emerge victorious in a competition, dispute, or challenging struggle.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi kadi takkar, vivad ya competition mein aakhri vijeta ban kar ubharna.
example: Despite aggressive opposition, the defense counsel came out on top in the appellate bench hearing.
contextNote: Competitive ya contested situations mein victory emphasize karta hai.
keyDistinction: 'Come out on top' jeetne ke liye hai; 'over the top' excessive ya natkiya vyavhar ke liye hai.

definition: To fail to achieve the intended result, accurate target, or expected standard.
hinglishExplanation: Apne lakshya ya sahi anuman se chuk jana; umeed ke mutabiq parinaam na milna.
example: The initial budget estimate missed the mark by nearly twenty percent.
contextNote: Target, estimation ya policy outcome ke failure ko denote karta hai.
keyDistinction: 'Miss the mark' target chukna hai; 'make one's mark' apni pehchan banana hai.

definition: To fail completely to produce the intended effect, laugh, or positive impression.
hinglishExplanation: Poori tarah be-asar ya asafal hona; koi asar na chhodna.
example: The administrative officer's attempt at humor fell flat during the solemn committee briefing.
contextNote: Jokes, speeches, presentations ya strategies ke complete failure par lagta hai.
keyDistinction: 'Fall flat' kisi prabhav ya speech ke asafal hone ke liye hai; 'fall through' kisi plan ya deal ke cancel hone ke liye hai.

definition: Having to start all over again from the beginning after a complete failure.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi plan ke fail hone ke baad dobara shuruat par pahunch jana.
example: When the database migration crashed without a backup, the IT team was back to square one.
contextNote: Wasted effort aur complete reset ki situation.
keyDistinction: 'Back to square one' failure ke karan majbooran reset hai; 'clean slate' naye sire se fresh start lena hota hai.

definition: To fail to get an answer, recall information, or achieve any constructive result.
hinglishExplanation: Kuch bhi yaad na aana ya talaash karne par koi nateeja na milna.
example: I tried to recall the precedent file number during the hearing, but I drew a blank.
contextNote: Mental block ya investigation mein zero output ke liye use hota hai.
keyDistinction: 'Draw a blank' yaad na aana hai; 'draw the line' kisi boundary ya seema ko tay karna hai.

definition: To fail to reach the required standard, quota, or expected goal.
hinglishExplanation: Zaroorat ya target se thoda peeche reh jana; kami reh jana.
example: The revenue recovery drive came up short of its quarterly target by several lakhs.
contextNote: Measurable goals ya targets mein kami rehne ko darshata hai.
keyDistinction: 'Come up short' kisi bhi target ke peeche rehne par lagta hai, sirf paise ke liye nahi.

definition: To show that you can deal successfully with an unexpectedly difficult situation or crisis.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi kathin chunauti ya achanak aayi mushkil ka datkar muqabla karna aur safal hona.
example: When the senior clerk fell ill on the inspection day, the assistant rose to the occasion flawlessly.
contextNote: High pressure ya crisis situations mein exceptional competence dikhana.
keyDistinction: 'Rise to the occasion' action/performance hai; 'on the rise' aam taur par statistical increase hota hai.

definition: To initiate an activity, project, or process to ensure ongoing momentum.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi process ya project ki shuruat karna taaki kaam aage badh sake.
example: Let us schedule a preliminary audit meeting to get the ball rolling on digitization.
contextNote: Action start karne aur momentum create karne ke context mein.
keyDistinction: 'Get the ball rolling' shuruat karna hai; 'keep the ball rolling' chal rahe kaam ko continue rakhna hai.

definition: To succeed in doing something difficult, improbable, or unexpected.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi behad mushkil ya namumkin se lagne wale kaam ko safal bana lena.
example: Despite stiff procedural hurdles, the young advocate managed to pull off an acquittal.
keyDistinction: 'Pull it off' task accomplish karna hai; 'pull through' bimari ya crisis se bbach nikalna hai.

definition: Proceeding in a way that is likely to lead to the correct answer, solution, or success.
hinglishExplanation: Sahi raste ya sahi direction mein aage badhna.
example: The investigator's line of inquiry proved that he was on the right track from day one.
keyDistinction: 'On the right track' sahi raste par hona hai; 'lose track' khayal na rehna ya rasta bhatak jana hai.

definition: To discover what is correct through personal painful experiences or mistakes rather than advice.
hinglishExplanation: Apni galtiyon ya kadvay anubhavon se sabak seekhna.
example: Having missed the tender submission deadline, the firm learned the hard way about punctuality.
keyDistinction: 'Learn the hard way' experience se seekhna hai; 'in the worst way' kisi cheez ki tivra ichha ke liye bolte hain.

definition: To work, study, or read late into the night.
hinglishExplanation: Raat bhar der tak jaagkar kadi mehnat ya padhai karna.
example: Aspirants must burn the midnight oil to cover the entire competitive syllabus thoroughly.
contextNote: Late-night dedicated work/study ko denote karta hai.
keyDistinction: 'Burn the midnight oil' der raat tak kaam karne ke liye hai; 'work against the clock' deadline pressure mein tezi se kaam karne ke liye hai.

definition: To make a special effort that goes beyond what is strictly required or expected.
hinglishExplanation: Apni zimmewari se aage badhkar zaroorat se zyada mehnat ya madad karna.
example: The dedicated court clerk always went the extra mile to assist litigants with complex forms.
keyDistinction: 'Go the extra mile' extra effort dalna hai; 'a mile a minute' bohot tez speed par bolne ya chalne ke liye hai.

definition: To do everything possible and explore every avenue in order to achieve a goal.
hinglishExplanation: Koi kasar na chhodna; har sambhav rasta apnana.
example: The special investigation team left no stone unturned to locate the absconding witness.
keyDistinction: 'Leave no stone unturned' poori koshish karna hai; 'stone's throw' nazdeeki distance ke liye hai.

definition: To continue doing something with persistence and determination despite difficulties.
hinglishExplanation: Mushkilon ke bawajood kisi kaam mein lagataar lage rehna.
example: Mastering complex English grammar is tough, but if you keep at it, results will follow.
keyDistinction: 'Keep at it' lagataar koshish karna hai; 'keep off' kisi cheez se door rehna hai.

definition: To try one's hardest and make the most positive personal impression possible.
hinglishExplanation: Apna best performance dena aur accha impression banane ki poori koshish karna.
example: During the oral interview, each candidate was determined to put their best foot forward.
contextNote: Interviews, presentations ya first encounters mein best effort.
keyDistinction: 'Put best foot forward' best impression dena hai; 'put one's foot down' kisi baat par sakhti se mana karna hai.

definition: To do one's full and fair share of work in a joint activity or collective group.
hinglishExplanation: Group ya team mein apne hisse ka poora kaam zimmedari se karna.
example: In a collaborative judicial audit, every officer must pull their weight to meet the deadline.
keyDistinction: 'Pull one's weight' apna hissa imaandari se karna hai; 'throw weight around' authority ka ghamand dikhana hai.

definition: To stop chatting or delaying and begin dealing with the serious, practical work at hand.
hinglishExplanation: Idhar-udhar ki baatein chhod kar seedhe mudde ya ahem kaam par aana.
example: After brief introductions, the administrative committee got down to business.
contextNote: Meeting ya session mein serious phase ka start.
keyDistinction: 'Get down to business' kaam shuru karna hai; 'mind own business' doosron ke mamle mein taang na adana hai.

definition: To be overwhelmed with an excessive amount of work, pending files, or obligations.
hinglishExplanation: Kaam ke bojh ke neeche dab jana; bohot zyada pending work hona.
example: Following the district restructuring, the registry staff was snowed under with pending petitions.
contextNote: Heavy workload aur time constraint ki situation.
keyDistinction: 'Snowed under' kaam ke bojh ke liye hai; 'under the weather' thoda beemar mehsoos karne ke liye hai.

definition: To work extremely fast in order to finish something before an imminent deadline.
hinglishExplanation: Deadline pass hone ke karan samay ke khilaf tezi se kaam karna.
example: The technical maintenance crew worked against the clock to restore the court network by morning.
contextNote: Urgency aur imminent deadline ka pressure.
keyDistinction: 'Against the clock' speed aur strict deadline par focus karta hai; 'midnight oil' der raat tak padhne/kaam karne par.

idiom: Go back to the drawing board
definition: To start designing or planning a project anew because the previous attempt failed.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi plan ke fail hone par dobara naye sire se strategy banana.
example: When the benchmark algorithm proved inadequate, the engineering team had to go back to the drawing board.
keyDistinction: 'Back to the drawing board' redesigning/replanning hai; 'across the board' sabhi par barabar lagu hone ke liye hai.

definition: To force oneself to face an unpleasant situation or undergo a painful ordeal with fortitude.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi aprasann ya mushkil kaam ko himmat ke saath jhelne ya swikar karne ka faisla karna.
example: The administration decided to bite the bullet and shut down the obsolete server cluster.
contextNote: Inevitable unpleasant task ko bina shikayat face karna.
keyDistinction: 'Bite the bullet' mushkili ko sehna hai; 'dodge a bullet' kisi bade khatre se baal-baal bachna hai.

idiom: Keep one's nose to the grindstone
definition: To work intensely and continuously without taking breaks or getting distracted.
hinglishExplanation: Bina ruke lagataar kadi mehnat karte rehna.
example: For six straight months, he kept his nose to the grindstone to clear the competitive examination.
contextNote: Relentless, disciplined labor over an extended period.
keyDistinction: 'Nose to grindstone' continuous hard work hai; 'turn up nose' kisi cheez ko heya drishti se reject karna hai.

definition: To put forward one's maximum possible effort and ability in an undertaking.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi kaam mein apni poori taqat aur koshish jhonk dena.
example: Even though the test was exceptionally tough, Ravi was determined to give it his best shot.
contextNote: Best personal effort irrespective of outcome.
keyDistinction: 'Give best shot' maximum effort hai; 'long shot' kam sambhavna wale chance ke liye use hota hai.

definition: In the final, concluding stage of a long task, journey, or arduous project.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi lambe safar ya project ke aakhri padav ya antim charan par hona.
example: With ninety percent of the files cataloged, the team felt they were finally on the home stretch.
contextNote: Final phase of an effort before completion.
keyDistinction: 'Home stretch' final stage hai; 'stretch the truth' baat ko badha-chadhakar jhooth bolna hai.

definition: To do something quickly or cheaply in an improper way by ignoring established standards.
hinglishExplanation: Paisa ya samay bachane ke liye galat tareeqe apnana ya quality se samjhauta karna.
example: Never cut corners while verifying official court records, as an oversight can result in contempt.
contextNote: Negative connotation: taking risky or unethical shortcuts.
keyDistinction: 'Cut corners' quality se compromise karke shortcut lena hai; 'cut short' kisi cheez ko waqt se pehle terminate karna hai.

definition: To disclose secret or confidential information prematurely or indiscreetly.
hinglishExplanation: Khabar ya raaz ko galti se ya samay se pehle ujagar kar dena.
example: The clerk accidentally spilled the beans about the confidential transfer list before the official gazette.
contextNote: Inadvertent or careless disclosure of private information.
keyDistinction: 'Spill the beans' raaz disclose karna hai; 'hear through grapevine' afwah ya anaupcharik sutron se sunna hai.

idiom: Let the cat out of the bag
definition: To reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi chhipayi hui baat ko anjaane mein sabke samne zaahir kar dena.
example: Her younger brother let the cat out of the bag about the surprise retirement celebration.
contextNote: Accidental revelation of a concealed surprise or plan.
keyDistinction: Dono similar hain; 'let the cat out of the bag' aksar surprise reveal karne ke context mein zyada dikhta hai.

definition: To keep something secret, confidential, or protected from public disclosure.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi jaankari ya plan ko gupt rakhna aur public mein na aane dena.
example: The high-level judicial inquiry report was kept strictly under wraps until tabled before the assembly.
keyDistinction: 'Keep under wraps' secrecy maintain karna hai; 'wrap head around' kisi complex concept ko samajhna hai.

definition: To discuss a matter without coming directly to the central, important point.
hinglishExplanation: Mukhya baat ko chhodkar idhar-udhar ki gol-mol baatein karna.
example: The witness was warned by the magistrate not to beat around the bush and answer the direct question.
contextNote: Indirectness, evasion, or reluctance to speak bluntly.
keyDistinction: 'Beat around the bush' aur 'get straight to the point' exact antonymous communicative behaviors hain.

definition: To address the most essential topic immediately without preamble or digression.
hinglishExplanation: Seedhe mukhya mudde par aana bina kisi faltu baatcheet ke.
example: Due to limited bench time, the presiding judge requested counsel to get straight to the point.
keyDistinction: 'Get straight to point' direct baat karna hai; 'miss the point' asal baat ko samajh na pana hai.

definition: To perceive an implied or unstated meaning that is not directly expressed in words.
hinglishExplanation: Chhipe huye arth ya ankahe bhaav ko samajhna.
example: If you read between the lines of the official circular, subtle policy revisions are evident.
contextNote: Inferring hidden meanings from formal texts or statements.
keyDistinction: 'Read between the lines' hidden meaning infer karna hai; 'cross the line' maryada ya boundary todna hai.

definition: To hear news or information through informal rumors, gossip, or unofficial channels.
hinglishExplanation: Afwahon ya anaupcharik baatchit ke zariye koi khabar sunna.
example: I heard it through the grapevine that the promotion examinations will be held in November.
keyDistinction: 'Grapevine' unverified gossip ya rumor ko emphasize karta hai; 'word of mouth' natural oral recommendations ke liye hota hai.

definition: To keep someone informed about developments and decisions concerning a matter.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi vyakti ko lagataar updates aur taaza jaankari se avagat rakhna.
example: Please ensure that the registrar is kept in the loop regarding all courtroom technology upgrades.
keyDistinction: 'In the loop' informed rehna hai; 'in the dark' kisi jaankari se anjaan rehna hai.

idiom: Get the wrong end of the stick
definition: To completely misunderstand or misinterpret a situation, explanation, or fact.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi baat ya situation ka poori tarah ulta ya galat matlab nikaal lena.
example: The auditor got the wrong end of the stick and thought funds were missing when they were simply reallocated.
keyDistinction: 'Wrong end of stick' galatfehmi hai; 'upper hand' advantage hasil karne ke liye hai.

definition: To falsely assert that someone has said something that they did not actually say.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi vyakti par aisi baat thopna jo usne asal mein nahi kahi ho.
example: The witness protested that the cross-examiner was putting words in her mouth.
confusedWith: Take the words out of mouth
keyDistinction: 'Put words in mouth' galat claim karna hai ki usne yeh kaha; 'take words out of mouth' vahi bolna jo doosra soch raha tha.

definition: To express one's opinions, feelings, or thoughts frankly and without fear.
hinglishExplanation: Bina kisi jhijhak ke saaf aur spasht roop se apni baat rakhna.
example: The senior advocate was respected because he always spoke his mind with impeccable honesty.
keyDistinction: 'Speak mind' khulkar bolna hai; 'lose mind' pagal ya be-kaabu ho jana hai.

definition: To reverse one's previous opinion, plan, decision, or emotional stance.
hinglishExplanation: Apna faisla, vichar ya bhavna poori tarah badal lena.
example: Initially opposed to the settlement, the complainant had a change of heart after counseling.
contextNote: Internal reconsideration leading to a modified position.
keyDistinction: 'Change of heart' decision/attitude ka badalna hai; 'at heart' mool swabhav ko kehte hain.

idiom: At the tip of one's tongue
definition: Almost recalled and about to be spoken, but not quite remembered at that exact moment.
hinglishExplanation: Baat ya naam dimaag mein hona lekin thik us waqt zuban par na aana.
example: The statute citation was on the tip of my tongue, but I had to check the legal digest.
keyDistinction: 'Tip of tongue' yaad na aane ki sthiti hai; 'slip of tongue' bolte waqt anjaane mein galti se galat bol jana hai.

definition: Communication passing informally from person to person through oral conversation.
hinglishExplanation: Ek vyakti se doosre vyakti tak aam baatchit ke madhyam se jaankari ka phailna.
example: The reputation of the coaching academy spread primarily through word of mouth among successful candidates.
keyDistinction: 'Word of mouth' aam communication ya recommendation hai; 'hearsay' legal context mein unadmissible afwah/secondary evidence hota hai.

definition: To defuse hidden tension, suspicion, or misunderstanding by open and honest discussion.
hinglishExplanation: Khulkar baatchit karke aapsi galatfehmi, tanaav ya shaq ko door karna.
example: A frank discussion between the union leaders and administration helped clear the air.
keyDistinction: 'Clear the air' misunderstandings suljhana hai; 'walk on air' behad khush mehsoos karna hai.

definition: To suddenly become intensely angry and fail to control one's emotional outburst.
hinglishExplanation: Achanak gusse par kaabu kho dena aur krodhit ho jana.
example: The presiding officer remained composed and never lost his temper even under severe provocation.
contextNote: Loss of self-control due to anger.
keyDistinction: Dono exact antonymous emotional behaviors represent karte hain.

definition: To remain calm, composed, and controlled in a difficult or provocative situation.
hinglishExplanation: Mushkil ya tanaavpoorn sthiti mein bhi shaant aur sanyamit bane rehna.
example: Despite aggressive questioning by the panel, the candidate kept her cool throughout.
keyDistinction: 'Keep cool' calmness aur composure hai; 'cold feet' dar ya ghabrahat ke karan peechhe hatna hai.

definition: Feeling unusually depressed, gloomy, or unhappy.
hinglishExplanation: Udaas, niraash ya be-jaan mehsoos karna.
example: After failing the preliminary exam by one mark, Ramesh was down in the dumps for weeks.
contextNote: Temporary state of mild dejection or sorrow.
keyDistinction: 'Down in dumps' udaasi hai; 'down to earth' vyavaharik aur vinamra vyakti ke liye use hota hai.

definition: Extremely happy, ecstatic, and joyful.
hinglishExplanation: Atyadhik khush hona; khushi ka thikana na rehna.
example: When she received her official appointment letter from the High Court, she was on cloud nine.
keyDistinction: 'On cloud nine' bohot khush hona hai; 'head in clouds' avyavaharik ya daydreaming karne wale ke liye hai.

definition: A nervous, fluttery feeling in the stomach before an important event or performance.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi ahem event ya pariksha se pehle ghabrahat ya bechaini mehsoos hona.
example: Standing outside the interview chamber, Suresh felt butterflies in his stomach.
contextNote: Anticipatory anxiety before a significant test or presentation.
keyDistinction: 'Butterflies in stomach' nervous tension hai; 'gut feeling' aantarik aabhas ya intuition hai.

definition: To suddenly lose courage and become too fearful to proceed with a planned action.
hinglishExplanation: Achanak dar jana aur aage badhne ki himmat kho dena.
example: The whistleblower got cold feet at the last minute and refused to sign the affidavit.
contextNote: Last-minute loss of nerve or hesitation.
keyDistinction: 'Cold feet' dar se pichhe hatna hai; 'keep cool' calmness banaye rakhna hai.

definition: An apparent misfortune or disappointment that ultimately brings unexpected benefits.
hinglishExplanation: Shuruat mein musibat lagne wali aisi ghatna jo aage chal kar faydemand sabit ho.
example: Failing the initial exam was a blessing in disguise, as it forced him to prepare far more rigorously for the judicial cadre.
contextNote: Silver lining behind an initial setback.
keyDistinction: 'Blessing in disguise' bura jo accha nikle; 'wolf in sheep's clothing' dhokhebaz vyakti jo shareef bane.

definition: To aggravate an already tense, angry, or contentious situation.
hinglishExplanation: Bhadke huye gusse ya tanaav ko aur zyada badhana; aag mein ghee daalna.
example: His arrogant remark only added fuel to the fire during the union negotiation.
contextNote: Escalating a conflict or emotional crisis.
keyDistinction: 'Add fuel to fire' tanaav badhana hai; 'clear the air' tanaav ko door karna hai.

idiom: Make a mountain out of a molehill
definition: To treat a trifling, minor matter as a catastrophic or serious problem.
hinglishExplanation: Chhoti si baat ka batangar banana; rai ka pahad banana.
example: It was merely a typographical error on the cover sheet; don't make a mountain out of a molehill.
keyDistinction: Dono similar hain; 'mountain out of molehill' vyakti ke overreaction ko denote karta hai, 'storm in teacup' event/commotion ko.

idiom: Have a chip on one's shoulder
definition: To harbour a persistent grudge, sense of grievance, or combative belligerence.
hinglishExplanation: Har waqt gusse mein rehna ya purani ranjish ke karan chid-chida vyavhar karna.
example: Ever since he was passed over for promotion, he has had a chip on his shoulder.
keyDistinction: 'Chip on shoulder' gussa aur ranjish hai; 'heart on sleeve' bhavnaon ko khule aam dikhana hai.

idiom: Wear one's heart on one's sleeve
definition: To display one's true emotions openly and candidly rather than concealing them.
hinglishExplanation: Apni bhavnaon ko bina chhupaye khule aam dikhana.
example: A judicial officer must remain impassive; you cannot wear your heart on your sleeve on the bench.
keyDistinction: 'Heart on sleeve' open emotional expression hai; 'chip on shoulder' chipa hua gussa/grudge hai.

definition: To be extremely delighted, overjoyed, and thrilled.
hinglishExplanation: Bohot zyada prashann aur uttsahit hona.
example: The entire village was over the moon when their local girl cracked the administrative service.
keyDistinction: 'Over the moon' khushi ki sthiti hai; 'once in a blue moon' durlabh frequency (rarely) ke liye hai.

definition: To remain cheerful, optimistic, and courageous in the face of misfortune or adversity.
hinglishExplanation: Bure waqt mein bhi hosla aur himmat banaye rakhna.
example: Keep your chin up; you have another attempt at the exam next year.
keyDistinction: 'Keep chin up' himmat rakhna hai; 'turn up nose' heya drishti dikhana hai.

definition: To persistently irritate, annoy, or provoke someone.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi ko lagataar pareshan ya irritate karte rehna.
example: The constant flickering of the old monitor was really getting on the clerk's nerves.
keyDistinction: Dono annoyance darshate hain; 'drive up wall' extreme frustration ke liye hai.

definition: An unpleasant or humiliating truth, event, or condition that must be accepted.
hinglishExplanation: Aisi kadvi sacchayi ya apriy sthiti jise majbooran swikar karna pade.
example: The loss of the senior standing in the roster was a bitter pill for the applicant to swallow.
keyDistinction: 'Bitter pill' kadvi sacchayi hai; 'sugarcoat' kadvi baat ko meethi karke pesh karna hai.

idiom: Cost an arm and a leg
definition: To be exorbitantly expensive or cost a prohibitive amount of money.
hinglishExplanation: Bahut zyada mehanga hona; bohot badi keemat chukana.
example: Importing proprietary server hardware for the district court costs an arm and a leg.
keyDistinction: 'Cost arm and leg' expensive item ke liye hai; 'live from hand to mouth' aamdan ki kami/garibi ke liye hai.

definition: To cost more money than one can afford or completely deplete one's financial reserves.
hinglishExplanation: Budget se bahar hona ya poori bachat khatam kar dena.
example: Purchasing good study books will help your career without breaking the bank.
contextNote: Affordability and budget constraints (often used in negative: won't break the bank).
keyDistinction: 'Break the bank' budget exhaust hona hai; 'make ends meet' basic survival expenses cover karna hai.

definition: To earn just enough income to cover basic living expenses.
hinglishExplanation: Itni aamdani hona jisse guzaara chal sake; kharche poore karna.
example: On a meager stipend, the young apprentice struggled to make ends meet in the capital city.
keyDistinction: 'Make ends meet' basic kharche manage karna hai; 'hand to mouth' bilkul saving na hona aur agle din ki chinta rehna hai.

definition: To have only just enough money to survive day to day without any savings for the future.
hinglishExplanation: Roz kamana aur roz khana; bhavishya ke liye koi bachat na hona.
example: Before securing regular government employment, his family had lived from hand to mouth for years.
contextNote: Acute poverty and absence of financial cushion.
keyDistinction: 'Hand to mouth' personal poverty ke liye hai; 'on a shoestring' tight budget par venture chalane ke liye hai.

definition: To reserve money or resources for an unforeseen emergency or future hardship.
hinglishExplanation: Mushkil waqt ya aapatkal ke liye bachat karke rakhna.
example: Prudent civil servants always save for a rainy day by investing in provident funds.
keyDistinction: 'Save for rainy day' bachat karna hai; 'rain on parade' kisi ki khushi ya plan ko kharab karna hai.

definition: Extremely valuable, immensely helpful, or of irreplaceable utility.
hinglishExplanation: Bahut zyada kimti, anmol ya faydemand hona.
example: An experienced stenographer who knows procedural drafting is worth their weight in gold.
keyDistinction: 'Worth weight in gold' anmol hone ke liye hai; 'golden handshake' retirement ke waqt badi severance package ke liye hai.

definition: Money is not easily acquired and must be earned through hard work; it is finite.
hinglishExplanation: Paisa ped par nahi ugta; paise ki qadr karni chahiye.
example: Turn off the lights when leaving the library; money doesn't grow on trees.
keyDistinction: Yeh caution/proverbial idiom hai financial waste ke khilaf.

definition: To cut back on spending and live on a reduced budget during financial hardship.
hinglishExplanation: Kharche kam karna aur sanyam se rehna; tangi ke waqt budget ghatana.
example: With inflation rising and revenues constrained, the department had to tighten its belt.
keyDistinction: 'Tighten belt' kharche ghatana hai; 'below the belt' anuchit ya anaitik vaar karne ke liye hai.

definition: To earn the livelihood that supports one's family or to achieve material success.
hinglishExplanation: Pariwar ke liye rozi-roti kamana ya kamyabi hasil karna.
example: As the primary earner, she worked diligently to bring home the bacon for her aging parents.
keyDistinction: 'Bring home bacon' aamdani kamana hai; 'save one's bacon' mushkil se jaan ya izzat bachana hai.

definition: To pay far more for something than its reasonable or fair market value.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi cheez ke liye hadd se zyada keemat chukana; loot jana.
example: Late filers often pay through the nose in late fees and penalties.
confusedWith: Cost an arm and a leg
keyDistinction: 'Cost arm and leg' item ki high cost batata hai; 'pay through nose' buyer dwara excessive payment karne ke act ko emphasize karta hai.

definition: Operating with a very small or severely restricted budget.
hinglishExplanation: Bohot kam budget ya seemit sansadhanon ke sahare kaam chalana.
example: The legal aid clinic operated on a shoestring budget but delivered justice to hundreds.
keyDistinction: 'On a shoestring' budget/venture ke liye hai; 'hand to mouth' household personal survival ke liye hai.

idiom: A penny saved is a penny earned
definition: Saving money that you have is as valuable as earning additional money.
hinglishExplanation: Bachaya hua paisa kamaye huye paise ke barabar hota hai.
example: By avoiding unnecessary printouts, the office saved thousands; truly, a penny saved is a penny earned.
keyDistinction: 'Penny saved' bachat ki prashansa hai; 'penny-wise' choti bachat karke bada nuksan karne ki aalochna hai.

definition: Occurring very rarely, infrequently, or on exceptional occasions.
hinglishExplanation: Kabhi-kabaar; bohot hi durlabh maukon par hona (Eid ka chaand).
example: The chief justice visits the subordinate court library once in a blue moon.
keyDistinction: 'Once in blue moon' frequency (rare) hai; 'over the moon' khushi ki state hai.

definition: At the very last possible moment, just before it is too late.
hinglishExplanation: Aen waqt par; theek antim kshan par pahunch jana.
example: The stay order petition was submitted in the nick of time before demolition commenced.
contextNote: Last moment arrival or prevention of a crisis.
keyDistinction: Dono similar hain; 'nick of time' rescue ya prevention par focus karta hai, 'eleventh hour' decision/action par.

definition: All day and all night without stopping; continuously twenty-four hours a day.
hinglishExplanation: Din-raat bina ruke lagataar; 24 ghante.
example: Technicians worked around the clock to restore the High Court network connectivity.
keyDistinction: 'Around the clock' 24 ghante continuity hai; 'against the clock' deadline beat karne ki race hai.

definition: At the latest possible time or final moment before an event occurs.
hinglishExplanation: Aakhri pal mein; antim moment par koi faisla ya badlav karna.
example: The government amended the notification at the eleventh hour, granting relief to candidates.
keyDistinction: 'Eleventh hour' aksar late decisions ke liye use hota hai; 'nick of time' critical rescue/entry ke liye.

definition: Time appears to pass astonishingly fast and quickly.
hinglishExplanation: Waqt ka pata hi na chalna; samay bohot tezi se beetna.
example: When you are engrossed in drafting, time flies without notice.
keyDistinction: 'Time flies' waqt ka tezi se nikalna hai; 'behind times' purane jamane ka hona hai.

definition: Having progressive ideas or technologies that are far more advanced than contemporary society.
hinglishExplanation: Apne samay se aage hona; bohot aadhunik ya pragatisheel hona.
example: The reformer's proposals on digital courtrooms in the 1980s were well ahead of their time.
contextNote: Visionary thinking that exceeds contemporary norms.
keyDistinction: Dono exact temporal opposites hain: advanced visionary vs obsolete backward.

definition: Almost instantaneously; very quickly and with minimal delay.
hinglishExplanation: Palak jhapakte hi; bohot hi kam samay mein.
example: With the new automated indexing system, the record room clerk located files in no time.
keyDistinction: 'In no time' speed (very quickly) darshata hai; 'nick of time' last moment arrival darshata hai.

definition: Old-fashioned, out-of-date, and failing to conform to contemporary standards.
hinglishExplanation: Purane jamane ka; samay ke sath na chalne wala.
example: Relying purely on manual registers makes the record division look behind the times.
keyDistinction: Opposite of ahead of one's time.

definition: To stop working on something for the rest of the day or temporarily cease an activity.
hinglishExplanation: Aaj ke liye kaam band karna ya chhutti lena.
example: After indexing five hundred case files, the exhausted team decided to call it a day.
keyDistinction: 'Call it a day' aaj ka kaam khatam karna hai; 'call it quits' kisi relationship ya project ko permanently band karna hai.

definition: To do something purely to pass the time while waiting for something else to happen.
hinglishExplanation: Waqt kaatna ya intezar karte waqt samay bitana.
example: While waiting for the bench to assemble, counsel read legal journals to kill time.
keyDistinction: 'Kill time' waqt pass karne ka conscious effort hai; 'time flies' waqt ka tezi se nikalna hai.

definition: Over an extended period of time; ultimately in the final analysis.
hinglishExplanation: Aage chal kar; lambe samay mein; aakhirkar.
example: Investing in computerized courtroom infrastructure will save enormous public money in the long run.
keyDistinction: 'Long run' extended future outcomes ke liye hai; 'short term' tatkalik parinam ke liye hai.

idiom: At the drop of a hat
definition: Willingly and immediately, without any hesitation or prior planning.
hinglishExplanation: Bina kisi hichkichahat ke turant; achanak bina deri kiye.
example: The dedicated staff was willing to work overtime at the drop of a hat during emergency sessions.
keyDistinction: 'At drop of a hat' instant willingness hai; 'once in blue moon' rare occurrence hai.

definition: To be in full agreement with someone on a matter.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi baat par poori tarah sehmat hona; ek jaisi rai rakhna.
example: The prosecution and defense did not see eye to eye on the admissibility of the electronic logs.
keyDistinction: 'See eye to eye' sehmat hona hai; 'turn blind eye' kisi galti ko jaanbujhkar ignore karna hai.

definition: To end a longstanding dispute, quarrel, or conflict and make peace.
hinglishExplanation: Purani dushmani ya jhagda bhula kar aapsi sulah kar lena.
example: After years of bitter litigation, the two business partners decided to bury the hatchet and settle out of court.
keyDistinction: 'Bury the hatchet' dushmani khatam karke sulah karna hai; 'see eye to eye' kisi point par aam rai hona hai.

definition: To do or say something that relieves social awkwardness or tension among strangers.
hinglishExplanation: Naye logon ke beech shuruati jhijhak ya khamoshi ko todna.
example: The chairperson shared a humorous anecdote to break the ice at the start of the inter-departmental meet.
keyDistinction: 'Break the ice' strangers ke beech awkwardness khatam karna hai; 'bury the hatchet' dushmano ke beech sulah karwana hai.

definition: To make an offer of peace, reconciliation, or conciliation to an adversary.
hinglishExplanation: Shanti ya dosti ka prastav aage badhana; dushmani mitane ki pehel karna.
example: The management extended an olive branch to the striking employees by offering mediation talks.
keyDistinction: 'Extend olive branch' dosti/sulah ka prastav hai; 'white flag' surrender ya haar maan lene ka prateek hai.

definition: Someone who offers sympathetic listening, emotional support, and comfort during distress.
hinglishExplanation: Aisa vyakti jo dukh ke waqt sahara bane aur dukh sun kar himmat de.
example: During her difficult family crisis, her colleague proved to be a reliable shoulder to cry on.
keyDistinction: 'Shoulder to cry on' empathy aur sahara hai; 'cold shoulder' jaanbujhkar ignore karna aur upeksha karna hai.

definition: To deliberately ignore, dismiss, or treat someone in an unfriendly, aloof manner.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi vyakti ko jaanbujhkar nazarandaz karna ya rukhapan dikhana.
example: After voting against the resolution, the council member was given the cold shoulder by his faction.
keyDistinction: 'Cold shoulder' kisi doosre ko ignore karna hai; 'cold feet' khud dar kar peechhe hatna hai.

definition: Under all circumstances, supporting someone through good times as well as severe hardships.
hinglishExplanation: Har acche aur bure waqt mein sath nibhana; sukh-dukh mein sath rehna.
example: True friends stand by each other through thick and thin.
keyDistinction: 'Thick and thin' loyalty through hardships hai; 'skin and bone' bohot kamzor vyakti ke physical state ke liye hai.

definition: To know someone or something thoroughly, intimately, and completely.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi vyakti ya vishay ko ragon-rag se poori tarah janna.
example: Having worked together for two decades, the senior partners knew each other inside out.
keyDistinction: 'Inside out' deep knowledge/familiarity hai; 'upside down' ulta hone ke liye hai.

definition: In stubborn, persistent dispute, disagreement, or confrontation with someone.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi ke sath aapas mein kadi tanaav, jhagde ya asahamati mein hona.
example: The bar association and the administrative committee are at loggerheads over courtroom allocation.
keyDistinction: Antonym of see eye to eye.

definition: Two people who are remarkably similar in appearance, tastes, character, or habits.
hinglishExplanation: Do log jo aapas mein bilkul ek jaise dikhte ya sochte hon; ek thaili ke chatte-batte.
example: The twin sisters both chose law and share the exact same study habits—they are like two peas in a pod.
keyDistinction: Dono similarity darshate hain; 'two peas in a pod' close binary pair ke liye zyada natural hai.

definition: To help or assist someone with an activity or difficult burden.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi ki madad karna ya hath batana.
example: Whenever a junior clerk struggles with formatting, the senior superintendent lends a hand.
keyDistinction: 'Lend a hand' madad karna hai; 'wash hands of' kisi mamle se apna palla jhad lena hai.

definition: To cooperate and work harmoniously as an integrated group toward a common objective.
hinglishExplanation: Ek sath milkar aapas mein sahyog karna aur kaam poora karna.
example: If the division pulls together, we can complete the pending audit before the high court vacation.
keyDistinction: 'Pull together' sahyog karna hai; 'pull apart' alag-alag karna ya todna hai.

definition: To act prematurely before the proper, authorized, or appropriate time.
hinglishExplanation: Waqt se pehle jaldbazi mein koi kadam utha lena.
example: The press jumped the gun by announcing the verdict before the bench had formally signed the judgment.
keyDistinction: 'Jump the gun' samay se pehle jaldbazi karna hai; 'bite the bullet' mushkil kaam ko endure karna hai.

definition: To proceed spontaneously and decide what to do according to circumstances as they develop, without a fixed plan.
hinglishExplanation: Pehle se plan na karke halat ke mutabiq mauke par faisla lena.
example: We don't know the exact questioning style of the committee, so we will have to play it by ear.
keyDistinction: 'Play by ear' flexibly decide karna hai; 'turn deaf ear' jaanbujhkar sunne se inkar karna hai.

definition: To commit oneself resolutely to a decisive, bold, and risky course of action after hesitation.
hinglishExplanation: Kafi soch-vichar ke baad aakhirkar koi bada aur risk-bhara kadam utha lena.
example: After years in a private firm, Ajay took the plunge and began full-time preparation for the judicial service.
contextNote: Decisive commitment to a major venture.
keyDistinction: 'Take the plunge' deliberate calculated bold commitment hai; 'jump the gun' bina soche samjhe waqt se pehle kadam uthana hai.

definition: To be indecisive, hesitant, or unable to choose between competing alternatives.
hinglishExplanation: Duvidha mein hona; faisla na kar pana.
example: The judge was in two minds about granting bail given the contradictory evidentiary submissions.
keyDistinction: 'In two minds' duvidha hai; 'speak one's mind' khulkar apni baat rakhna hai.

definition: To delay making a decision or refuse to take sides in a dispute or controversy.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi paksh ka sath na lena aur faisla lene mein der karna; tatasth rehna.
example: On this vital administrative reform, the department head cannot sit on the fence any longer.
keyDistinction: 'Sit on fence' side lene se bachna hai; 'cross bridge' samay aane par problem deal karna hai.

idiom: The ball is in your court
definition: It is now your responsibility or turn to take action, make a move, or decide.
hinglishExplanation: Ab agla kadam uthane ya faisla lene ki baari aapki hai.
example: We have submitted the formal settlement draft; now the ball is in their court.
contextNote: Transfer of agency/initiative to the other party.
keyDistinction: 'Ball in court' agla kadam uthane ki responsibility hai; 'drop the ball' galti karke mauka gava dena hai.

definition: A policy, decision, or tool that has both favourable benefits and severe potential hazards.
hinglishExplanation: Dodhāri talwar; aisi cheez jiska fayda bhi ho aur bara nuksan bhi ho sakta ho.
example: Strict biometric attendance is a double-edged sword: it enforces discipline but harms morale.
contextNote: Dual nature of an option involving intrinsic risk.
keyDistinction: Dual consequence vs starting over.

definition: To attempt to deal with a matter and inadvertently uncover a complex web of unforeseen problems.
hinglishExplanation: Kisi aisi samasya ko chhedna jisse naye aur jatil vivad khade ho jayein.
example: Auditing that dormant project opened a can of worms regarding past financial irregularities.
keyDistinction: Dono similar hain; dono unforeseen cascading problems ke liye use hote hain.

definition: To confront and accept the unpleasant consequences or criticism of one's actions.
hinglishExplanation: Apni galti ka parinam ya daant-phatkār swikar karna; anjaam bhugatna.
example: Having fabricated the dispatch register, the errant clerk had to face the music before the vigilance committee.
keyDistinction: 'Face the music' anjaam bhugatna hai; 'music to ears' khushi dene wali khabar sunna hai.

idiom: Put all one's eggs in one basket
definition: To risk all of one's resources or hopes on a single venture or course of action.
hinglishExplanation: Apna sab kuch kisi ek hi plan ya risk par laga dena.
example: Never put all your eggs in one basket; prepare for both clerical and judicial stream exams.
keyDistinction: 'Put eggs in basket' concentration of risk hai; 'nest egg' emergency ke liye jod kar rakha hua fund hai.

definition: To deliberately pretend not to notice misconduct, rule violations, or an unpleasant reality.
hinglishExplanation: Jaanbujhkar kisi galti ya aniyamitata ko dekh kar bhi andekha karna.
example: The supervisory officer was suspended for turning a blind eye to procedural lapses.
keyDistinction: 'Turn blind eye' ignore karna hai; 'see eye to eye' sehmat hona hai.

definition: To speak frankly, bluntly, and directly about something, even if it is unpleasant.
hinglishExplanation: Bina kisi laag-lapet ke sach ko sach aur jhooth ko jhooth bolna.
example: In administrative reviews, the chief auditor preferred to call a spade a spade.
keyDistinction: Antonym of beat around the bush.

definition: A small, visible part of a much larger and more complicated hidden problem.
hinglishExplanation: Badi samasya ka sirf chhota sa dikhne wala hissa.
example: The initial audit shortage of ten thousand rupees was merely the tip of the iceberg.
keyDistinction: 'Tip of iceberg' chipe huye bade problem ka sanket hai; 'drop in ocean' kisi bade total ke samne insignificant amount hai.

definition: To avoid re-opening an old dispute or dormant issue that could cause fresh trouble.
hinglishExplanation: Gade murde na ukhadna; purane shaant mamle ko dobara chhed kar musibat na badhana.
example: The matter was resolved amicably last year, so it is best to let sleeping dogs lie.
contextNote: Avoiding unnecessary provocation of past controversies.
keyDistinction: 'Let sleeping dogs lie' purana vivad na chhedna hai; 'bark up wrong tree' galat direction mein talaash karna hai.

definition: To form an opinion or judgment hastily before having all the pertinent facts.
hinglishExplanation: Bina poore tathya jaane jaldbazi mein nateeja nikal lena.
example: Do not jump to conclusions about the missing record before the inquiry officer inspects the vault.
keyDistinction: 'Jump to conclusions' mental judgment hasty hona hai; 'jump the gun' physical action waqt se pehle lena hai.

idiom: Put one's foot in one's mouth
definition: To inadvertently say something tactless, embarrassing, or offensive.
hinglishExplanation: Anjaane mein aisi baat bol dena jisse sharmindgi ho ya doosre ko bura lage.
example: I really put my foot in my mouth when I criticized the report in front of its author.
contextNote: Social faux pas or blunder in conversation.
keyDistinction: 'Foot in mouth' embarrassing remark bolna hai; 'foot down' firmly mana karna hai.

idiom: The pot calling the kettle black
definition: A situation where someone accuses another of a fault that they themselves possess.
hinglishExplanation: Ulta chor kotwal ko daante; khud vahi kami hote huye doosre par ilzam lagana.
example: For the chronic latecomer to criticize my punctuality is truly the pot calling the kettle black.
confusedWith: Two wrongs don't make a right
keyDistinction: 'Pot calling kettle black' hypocrisy dikhata hai; 'two wrongs' badla lene ki galat soch ko roka jata hai.

definition: Strictly following all established official rules, laws, and regulations.
hinglishExplanation: Niyamon ka kaddai se palan karte huye kaam karna.
example: The registrar conducted the recruitment process strictly by the book to avoid legal challenges.
keyDistinction: 'By the book' rules follow karna hai; 'in good books' kisi ki nazar mein pasandeeda hona hai.

idiom: Bite off more than one can chew
definition: To undertake a task or commitment that is far too large or complex for one's capabilities.
hinglishExplanation: Apni aukaat ya kshamata se zyada kaam apne sar le lena.
example: By volunteering to manage three district audits simultaneously, the junior officer bit off more than he could chew.
keyDistinction: 'Bite off more than chew' overcommitment hai; 'bite the bullet' unpleasant situation ko endure karna hai.

idiom: The writing is on the wall
definition: Clear, undeniable indications that imminent failure, disaster, or downfall is going to happen.
hinglishExplanation: Spasht sanket hona ki bura anjaam ya downfall aane hi wala hai.
example: With multiple adverse judicial remarks, the writing was on the wall for the compromised agency.
keyDistinction: 'Writing on wall' obvious disaster ka warning sign hai; 'read between lines' subtle hidden meaning infer karna hai.
